transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Evan Cole (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Samira Patel (Redwood CSM); Alex Rivera, Priya Shah, Tom Wu, Sara Levin (Lighthouse Data)

Auto-generated Summary: 
- Purpose: SOC 2 / ISO27001 posture readout and plan for Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO flows, and KMS integration.
- Outcome: Redwood to share SOC2 docs, runbook and demo; Lighthouse to confirm trust-center users and residency requirements; schedule deeper RBAC walkthrough and pilot.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II evidence, ISO27001 mapping, Trust Center access provisioning, RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC), KMS/HSM integration and key management, audit log retention and export, data residency and isolation, pen test evidence, on-prem/private options.

[00:00] Evan Cole: Hey folks, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick readout of our compliance posture and then focus on the access plan for the trust center, RBAC flows, and KMS questions. Samira, want to kick off?
[00:20] Samira Patel: Yeah sure. Hi everybody from Lighthouse, appreciate the time. Quick agenda: SOC 2 artifacts, ISO mapping, how you can access evidence in the Trust Center, and then Maya will demo RBAC and KMS integration examples.
[00:35] Alex Rivera: Great. Our main goal today is just to validate scope: which systems are covered in Redwood's SOC2/ISO artifacts and get clarity on the support model for keys and audit logs. Also timeline: we want to finalize vendor due diligence by mid-September.
[00:50] Priya Shah: Hi, quick context — we run most workloads in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, and have a requirement for data residency in eu-west-1 for some regulated data sets. We'll need to understand if tokens or logs ever traverse outside region.
[01:10] Maya Lin: Super helpful. On residency, Redwood's hosted API stores customer data in assigned regions; we also offer Dedicated and Private deployments if you need air-gapped or VPC-only. That said, our Trust Center and control evidence are centralized — access is tenant-scoped, we can provision region-limited views.
[01:35] Tom Wu: Can you clarify encryption at rest — specifically, is customer data encrypted with customer-managed keys (BYOK) or Redwood-managed keys? And do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[01:50] Evan Cole: Short answer: both models are supported depending on plan. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default; Dedicated and Private can be configured with customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM integrations. We'll put details in the runbook.
[02:05] Alex Rivera: Ok, we'll need architecture diagrams and a matrix showing which deployment option supports BYOK, HSM, and what the operational responsibilities are.
[02:18] Maya Lin: Noted. We'll add a matrix and include sample CloudFormation/IaC snippet for KMS binding.
[02:30] Sara Levin: From legal perspective: we need the redacted pen test and SOC 2 Type II report. Also, do you have subprocessor lists and contracts?
[02:45] Samira Patel: Yes, subprocessor list is in the Trust Center; we will upload the redacted pen test summary and SOC2 report there. For contract language, we have a standard DPA and addendum — Samira to share.
[03:00] Alex Rivera: Awesome. On RBAC — we need to make sure Lighthouse's role model (admin, security reviewer, analyst) maps neatly and that audit logs show role changes and who assumed privileged roles.
[03:18] Maya Lin: Demo incoming — I'll share my screen in a second. Our RBAC supports fine-grained roles, SAML SSO mapping to groups, and an audit trail for role assignments and token issuance. There's occasional lag in the UI, but you can stream logs into your SIEM via our logs export API.
[03:40] [screen share noises] Maya Lin: So, here is the Admin console — you can create custom roles, set least privilege, and assign teams. We also emit event logs with object-level actions; note the event names are sometimes abbreviated in the audit stream (e.g., role_grant -> role:grant), I know transcription often swaps that.
[04:05] Priya Shah: For SSO we use Okta and Azure AD — SAML is preferred. How much of the mapping is automatic? We don't want to hand manage mappings across 50 teams.
[04:20] Maya Lin: We support group-to-role syncs via SCIM for Okta and Azure AD; SAML can map attributes too. SCIM provisioning is recommended for larger orgs to avoid manual map drift.
[04:35] Alex Rivera: Good. About audit logs retention — what's the default? We need 2 years for compliance.
[04:48] Evan Cole: Default hosted retention is 90 days; extended retention and log archival to customer-owned S3 is available on Dedicated/Enterprise plans. We can also provide stream to your SIEM in near-real time.
[05:05] Tom Wu: So if we need 2 years we would be on a Dedicated plan? Any options for hosted customers to get the same retention?
[05:18] Evan Cole: We can offer add-on retention for hosted accounts in enterprise contracts, but Dedicated gives you more control and predictable throughput. We'll run cost estimates for both in the follow-up.
[05:30] [slight crosstalk, someone drops connection briefly]
[05:50] Priya Shah: Clarify the trust center access model: can we scope which Lighthouse people see what artifacts? We have legal folks who shouldn't see raw logs.
[06:05] Samira Patel: Yes — Trust Center provisioning is role-based. You can map who sees SOC2 reports, pen test summaries, and who can download KMS audit keys. We'll need a list of users and scopes to provision properly.
[06:20] Alex Rivera: We'll send the initial list. Also, is there an SLA around evidence delivery when auditors request data?
[06:35] Evan Cole: We have an evidence delivery SLA for enterprise customers: 3 business days for routine requests; urgent items can be expedited with dedicated support. We'll include that in the materials.
[06:50] Priya Shah: For KMS integration, how are keys rotated and who has access to key material? Any chance keys ever leave AWS KMS boundary?
[07:05] Maya Lin: Keys stay within the provider boundary — if you use AWS KMS CMK with HSM, Redwood never has access to plaintext keys. Rotation can be automated via AWS KMS policies; we can show example IAM and KMS policies in the repo.
[07:20] Tom Wu: Pen test question — do you do continuous vuln scanning or annual assessments only?
[07:33] Evan Cole: We do regular vulnerability scanning and annual third-party pentests; we'll provide the executive summary and remediation timeline in the Trust Center.
[07:45] Alex Rivera: About ISO27001 mapping — do you provide a controls traceability matrix that maps RFC/controls to your SOC2 tests and evidence?
[08:00] Maya Lin: Yes we have a controls mapping doc mapping ISO27001 clauses to our SOC 2 control tests and evidence artifacts. We'll share the matrix as a spreadsheet in the Trust Center.
[08:15] Sara Levin: Any carve-outs or scope exclusions in your ISO/SOC coverage we should be aware of?
[08:25] Samira Patel: The reports include a scope statement; typical exclusions are customer-managed SaaS connectors or on-prem agents. We'll highlight those in the readout.
[08:40] Priya Shah: Network segmentation — do you have tenancy-level isolation and private networking for dedicated? We need to avoid any cross-tenant KV cache effects.
[08:55] Maya Lin: Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU pools and VPC peering options. The KV cache is scoped per-tenant; we've had incidents where transcription written as K V cache before, but rest assured it's tenant-scoped and encrypted.
[09:15] Alex Rivera: Can we get a small architecture diagram showing data flow for hosted vs dedicated vs private? That would help our risk team.
[09:25] Evan Cole: Absolutely. We'll attach diagrams, and we can also provide sample VPC endpoints for dedicated deployments.
[09:40] [longer silence while people skim attachments]
[10:05] Priya Shah: One operational ask — if we need to rotate an external key, what's the process and expected downtime?
[10:20] Maya Lin: Key rotation when orchestrated correctly can be seamless; we use double-write epochs for KV and token caches to avoid invalidation. Worst-case, a few seconds of increased latency per request while caches repopulate. We'll document the rotation playbook.
[10:40] Tom Wu: Are there known perf impacts during rotation or when using encrypted models and quantization? Not critical for us but good to know.
[10:55] Maya Lin: Some minor latency delta with customer-managed HSM keys due to crypto calls, but we can benchmark for you. If latency is a hard SLO, we recommend Dedicated with local KMS or a hybrid design.
[11:15] Alex Rivera: Ok, timeline and decision points — we need SOC2 docs and runbooks this week; then an RBAC deep dive and pilot next week.
[11:30] Samira Patel: We'll aim to get SOC2 and pen test summary into Trust Center by Friday 2026-09-05. Maya will draft RBAC runbook and schedule the hands-on demo for the week of 2026-09-08.
[11:50] Evan Cole: Any blockers on procurement or legal before we give broader access?
[12:00] Sara Levin: We need the DPA and subprocessors list; once redlined, we can approve Trust Center access for reviewers. We'll share comments by 2026-09-06.
[12:15] Alex Rivera: Final question: do you have a SOC 2 bridging letter for in-between audits?
[12:25] Samira Patel: We can provide a bridge letter summarizing changes since last report; we'll include that as an addendum in the Trust Center.
[12:40] [wrap-up noises]
[12:50] Evan Cole: Quick recap of next steps — we'll do: upload reports, share diagrams and RBAC runbook, estimate log-retention costs for hosted vs dedicated, and schedule RBAC walkthrough.
[13:05] Priya Shah: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[13:15] Alex Rivera: Thanks, appreciate it.
[13:25] Samira Patel: Thanks — I'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
[13:30] End of meeting.

Recorded action summary (auto): 1) Redwood to upload SOC2 and pen test summary to Trust Center. 2) RBAC runbook & demo to be shared. 3) Customer to provide residency and user lists.
